attempt: The relaxation oscillator frequency drift with temperature is a known issue. The probe capacitance changes with temperature, and the oscillator's RC time constant is temperature-dependent. Solutions: (1) Use a reference capacitor on the same PCB for differential measurement, (2) Temperature-compensate in software using a temp sensor, (3) Use a more stable oscillator topology like a 555 with precision resistors, (4) Calibrate at multiple temperatures and interpolate. The Pico's counting is fine at 800kHz.

title: Would it be possible to solder 2 6 layer pcb's on top of each other to get a cheap 6 layer pcb for large BGA fanouts?
attempt: Soldering two 6-layer PCBs together is mechanically possible but electrically problematic. Issues: (1) CTE mismatch between boards causes solder joint fatigue, (2) No reliable inter-layer connections without vias/plated holes, (3) Heat from soldering can delaminate inner layers, (4) Signal integrity across the joint will be poor. Better: use board-to-board connectors, or design as single 12-layer board, or use flex interconnect.

title: If I am driving a gate of a PMOS that already has 100 V on it, will the gate driver be able to drive it to 90 V with a 10 V output or will it break?
attempt: Driving PMOS gate with 100V on source: The gate must be pulled to source voltage to turn OFF (Vgs=0), and pulled ~10-15V BELOW source to turn ON (Vgs=-10 to -15V). Standard gate drivers (IR2110, etc.) handle this with bootstrap supply. If using MCU directly: need level shifter. 100V exceeds most gate driver ratings - use high-voltage gate driver (e.g., IX21844) or isolated driver. Check Vgs max rating (±20V typical).
